name: can_fling
notes: The flip attempt: plays FROM can_pickup's final carrying pose (offsets here are relative to that hold). Small downward wind-up, then joint3+joint4 drive the tip up as fast as the velocity cap allows (~22 deg/s per joint — enforce_velocity_cap stretches anything hotter, so the fling energy is whatever the safety cap permits, no more) and the jaws open 84->88% ABSOLUTE (63.8->66.9 mm, past the 66 mm can) in the final 0.35 s of the rise at 11.4 %/s — the HARDWARE gripper cap is 12 %/s, so opening any further in that window would stretch the segment and kill the fling's speed; the remaining open to 98% happens during the apex hold. The can releases with whatever upward speed the capped motion carries. The can tumbling instead of landing is the expected and disclosed outcome. Apex jaw tip ~45 cm up (URDF-checked); apex absolute joints from the measured rest: j2 30, j3 34, j4 37.6 — all inside soft limits. Excursions from motion start (the carrying pose): j3 +26 (budget 60), j4 -6/+27 (55); j2 never moves. Every waypoint's offset is >= 0 on joint2/joint3, and the gesture ENDS AT ITS OWN START POSE — measured on hardware, the arm sags a few degrees under gravity from the commanded carry (j2 27.6 vs 30, j3 at its 0 floor), so any 'undo the pickup' offset resolves BELOW the 0.0 soft floors and is refused; returning to the measured start is legal from wherever the arm actually is. The wind-up dip lives entirely in joint4 (floor -97). JOINT1 ZERO IN EVERY WAYPOINT (base clamped).

waypoints.label: release — jaws pass the can's 66 mm at full rise speed
hold the apex, finish opening — watch it land or not
return to the carrying pose, jaws neutral
